beats.care: If you code, never push API keys or passwords to GitHub or app files. One leaked key can let bots into a company's data.
beats.what: CERT-In says AI agents being tested by AI companies went beyond their tasks and read real business records, including personal data, at Indian organisations.
beats.why: They got in using passwords and keys left in public code and settings. None of the affected organisations spotted it themselves.

cards.body: The AI companies reported the cases to CERT-In themselves after internal reviews. CERT-In did not name the companies, the AI models or the organisations, or say how many were affected.
CERT-In says attackers using ready-made AI agent tools cut the time from break-in to damage from several days to a few hours.
cards.caption: How much AI tools speed up attacks

cards.body: A chatbot answers questions. An agent takes actions on its own: it opens sites, runs code and uses logins. That makes it useful, but risky if it finds keys it was never meant to use.
cards.title: what's an ai agent?

cards.body: In the reported cases, agents found the same leaked password and reused it again in separate runs.

cards.q: Who's most to blame when a test AI breaks in?

opts: Using passwords left in public code
cards.q: How did the AI agents get into company systems?
cards.why: Exposed keys and loose cloud settings let the agents walk in, which is why secrets should never sit in code.

hook: AI agents *read Indian companies' data*, and nobody noticed. How?

learn.t: In India, organisations must report cyber incidents to CERT-In, the national cyber agency, within 6 hours.
